rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God teaches His specially favored servants this supplication and alerts them that the way of conduct is necessary for arrival.
rows.anchor: تلقيناً لأهل لطفه وتنبيهاً على محل السلوك الذي لا وصول بدونه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali glosses guidance as returning the strayer to what he had lost.
rows.anchor: والهدى قال الحرالي : مرجع الضال إلى ما ضل عنه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali describes the path as a perilous road of conduct.
rows.anchor: مرجع الضال إلى ما ضل عنه ،   والصراط الطريق الخطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is God's own speech, placed on the tongues of the most eminent of His creation.
rows.anchor: والآية من كلام الله تعالى على لسان العُلّية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article identifies the uniquely encompassing path, whose guided traveler does not go astray because its scope is comprehensive.
rows.anchor: وجاء مكملاً بكلمة  "  أل  "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path encompasses the whole, while opinions and sects fragment when they incline toward one of its sides.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي تشتت الآراء وتفرقت الفرق بالميل إلى واحد من جانبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its likeness is the visible bridge over Hell on Judgment Day, lined with hooks; people's passage there follows how they traveled among its truths during worldly life.
rows.anchor: جهنم يوم الجزاء للعيان وتحفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī distinguishes praiseworthy lack of orientation, arising from sound nature and calling for restraint, from blameworthy deviation after guidance, arising from a crooked disposition.
rows.anchor: وهذا الصراط الأكمل وهو المحيط المترتب على الضلال الذي يعبر به عن حال من لا وجهة له ،   وهو ضلال ممدوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appositional restatement confirms that the straight way comes only through God's favor and signals that clinging to it means following His messengers.
rows.anchor: ثم أكد سبحانه وتعالى الإخبار بأن ذلك لن يكون إلا بإنعامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's blessing reaches every existent, ally or enemy; omitting what was bestowed generalizes the blessing while concentrating the request on its special recipients.
rows.anchor: لكل موجود عدواً كان أو ولياً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suppressing the object of bestowed makes the wording shorter while expanding its meaning through generalization.
rows.anchor: وكان حذف المنعم به لإرادة التعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Egypt and Damascus example distinguishes coordination, which excludes the second group from the first, from ghayr, which treats the excluded wrongdoers as part of the first group.
rows.anchor: اتبع طريق أهل مصر مثلاً لا أهل دمشق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since existence itself is a blessing and everyone follows some human path, the request must mean those specially favored with God's mercy, whose opposites are then identified as a warning.
rows.anchor: فعرف أن المسؤول إنما هو طريق أهل النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rejected group is destined for misery and deliberately fails in action, thereby deserving wrath.
rows.anchor: قسم أريد للشقاوة فعاند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other group was not destined for felicity and falls into ruin through neglect of knowledge.
rows.anchor: من جهة إخلاله بالعلم فصار إلى العطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning these groups after hope inspires fear alongside hope and clarifies that the intended blessing is the special grace given to the honored.
rows.anchor: ليكمل الإيمان بالرجاء والخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people under wrath are those whom God treats as an angry person treats the object of his anger.
rows.anchor: أي الذين تعاملهم معاملة الغضبان لمن وقع عليه غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr is made definite by annexation to its opposite and serves as an adjective for those who were blessed, like motion being other than rest.
rows.anchor: صفة للذين بإضافتها إلى الضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayr conveys negation rather than an exception: the wording excludes those characterized by the trait from the outset and avoids suggesting a merely lesser class.
rows.anchor: بدء على إخراج المتلبس بالصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The contrast shows the great blessing of the first group: there is no salvation without following them, and deliberate or mistaken departure brings misery, so the earnest should pursue their traces.
rows.anchor: وأنه لا نجاة إلا باتباعهم وأن من حاد عن سبيلهم عامداً أو مخطئاً شقي

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the wrathful openly show contrariness and deliberate opposition, bringing wrath from above and hatred from below.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : { المغضوب عليهم } الذين ظهر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali defines the strayers as people who faced a direction of guidance and veered away without intending to do so.
rows.anchor: وجهوا وجهة هدى فزاغوا عنها من غير تعمد لذلك

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali analyzes amīn as a word of resolve rooted in security, expressing confidence that the one invoked will not reject the caller.
rows.anchor: كلمة عزم{[287]} من الأمن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Only God can be called upon with this confidence, since every other being is subject to inability or obstruction.
rows.anchor: وهي{[288]} لا تصلح إلا لله لأن ما دونه لا ينفك عن عجز أو منع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amīn is a vocal form named for the imperative meaning respond.
rows.anchor: وهو صوت سمي به الفعل الذي هو استجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending loops back to the opening invocation of God's name: the first group gains mercy, while the two deviant groups join Satan's party and incur punishment.
rows.anchor: من حزب الشيطان فأخذتهم النقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Fātiḥa's order is obligatory, reversing its parts or inserting material not belonging to it invalidates prayer by disrupting the arrangement.
rows.anchor: الفاتحة في الصلاة لكونها واجبة في الترتيب

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī says the Qur'an's clearest pillar of inimitability lies in its arrangement and sequence.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : فإن القرآن معجز والركن الأبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī pictures the worshipper passing through unveiled majesty, annihilation of the transient, and visions of many perilous paths, then realizing that only God's guidance, care, and mercy bring safety.
rows.anchor: وعلم أن لا نجاة إلا بهدايته ولا عصمة بغير عنايته ولا سعادة إلا برحمته ولا سلامة لغير أهل نعمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing these realities, the worshipper answers the implied question about what to seek and where to go by asking for the straight path.
rows.anchor: كأنه قيل له : ماذا تطلب وفي-{[283]} أي مذهب تذهب ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having requested the noblest way, the worshipper asks for its best companions; because blessing may be worldly, he seeks protection from confused or unjust wanderers.
rows.anchor: ولما طلب أشرف طريق سأل أحسن رفيق فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following disavowal specifies that the requested blessing is not merely worldly, asking refuge from those wandering in confusion or injustice.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت النعمة قد تخص الدنيوية عينها واستعاذ{[284]} من أولئك

rows.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī organizes all blessings into first and second creation and preservation, respectively in the transient world and the abiding afterlife.
rows.anchor: كما قال العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي . إلى جميع النعم فإنها ترجع إلى إيجاد وإبقاء

rows.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
rows.claim: The first creation is named in praise of God, since bringing creatures from nonexistence into existence is the greatest nurturing.
rows.anchor: أما الإيجاد الأول فبقوله { الحمد لله رب العالمين } فإن الإخراج

rows.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
rows.claim: The first preservation is signaled by the Merciful, the Compassionate, whose great and subtle gifts sustain life.
rows.anchor: وأما الإبقاء الأول فبقوله : { الرحمن الرحيم } أي المنعم بجلائل النعم

rows.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
rows.claim: The second creation, in the afterlife, is signaled by the Master of the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: الإيجاد الثاني

rows.speaker: العلامة سعد الدين مسعود ابن عمرو التفتازاني الشافعي
rows.claim: The second preservation is signaled by worship through the end of the sūra, whose benefits return to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وأما الإبقاء الثاني فبقوله : { إياك نعبد } إلى آخرها ،   فإن منافع ذلك تعود إلى الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says the four later sūras that open with praise point, in sequence, to these four kinds of blessing; Biqāʿī will discuss them at their openings.
rows.anchor: ثم جاء التصدير بالحمد بعد الفاتحة في أربع سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the root sense of praise turns on reaching the utmost end, entailing expansiveness, encompassing scope, and perhaps humility, satisfaction, and gratitude.
rows.anchor: مادته بكل ترتيب تدور على بلوغ الغاية ويلزم منه الاتساع والإحاطة والاستدارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening praise moves from a particular expression toward the universal, explaining why consequential matters begin with praise; the relation of praise to gratitude is revisited in Sūrat al-Naḥl and Sabaʾ.
rows.anchor: بان سر الافتتاح بها من حيث تصديرها بالحمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divine names that follow praise encompass the Qur'an's theoretical doctrines and practical rulings, so the brief Fātiḥa is the Qur'an's mother and title, whose contents the rest unfolds.
rows.anchor: معاني القرآن من الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية فهي أم القرآن

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says God's entire great message is gathered in the seven oft-repeated verses, hidden beneath the Throne until the completion of creation and the final manifestation of praise through Muhammad.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو الحسن الحرالي في مفتاح الباب المقفل لفهم القرآن المنزل في آخر الباب التاسع منه : ولننه هذه الأبواب بذكر القرآن ومحتواه على الكتب

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali maps the stages of creation's unfolding onto successive scrolls, books, and tablets: scrolls concern what changes quickly, books what endures, and tablets what lasts for a time.
rows.anchor: فالصحف لما يتبدل سريعاً ،   والكتاب لما يثبت ويدوم أمداً

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali assigns Torah worldly legal penalties, the Gospel principles pointing beyond them to the kingdom, and the Psalms ecstatic praise; the Qur'an includes selections from each mode.
rows.anchor: وفي الإنجيل أصول تلك الأحكام

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the Qur'an gathers these scriptural modes, perfects blessing and religion, and completes the work, citing the completion of religion and the Prophet's mission to perfect noble character.
rows.anchor: من جميع وجوهه ،   فصار قرآناً جامعاً

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: The Qur'an develops detailed material in scattered revelations, whereas the seven concise, comprehensive principles of the Mother of the Qur'an are ordered one by one, sufficient without excess or deficiency.
rows.anchor: أن القرآن مقصود تنزيله التفصيل والجوامع

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali sees the Fātiḥa as God's disclosure from the beginning of dominion to praise, and the servants' progress from disavowing error to the straight path; the Qur'an gathers their relation.
rows.anchor: من بدء الملك إلى ختم الحمد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali describes the Qur'an's clear, glorious, generous, and wise aspects through audible verses, tested rulings, varied gifts, and the order of creation according to revelation.
rows.anchor: ومن كريمه وهو ما ظهرت فيه أفانين إنعامه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali distinguishes gradual revelation that moves between conditions and rulings as tanzīl from inzāl, which descends from high to low; inzāl has no intermediaries, while tanzīl does.
rows.anchor: من حال إلى حال وحكم إلى حكم كان تنزيلاً

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says Qur'anic explanation is embodied by the active exemplar in his deeds and character, while recitation is arranged according to the needs that arise.
rows.anchor: وبيانه حيث الإمام العامل به مظهره في أفعاله وأخلاقه كان خلقه القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī identifies the warning to fear the day of return to God as the last verse revealed.
rows.anchor: آخر آية أنزلت { واتقوا يوماً ترجعون فيه إلى الله

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly instructed that the verse about the day of return be placed between the verse of debt and the verse before it, illustrating that chronological existence and Qur'anic ordering may differ.
rows.anchor: "  اجعلوها بين آية الدين والآية التي قبلها  "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī illustrates this distinction with 33:50, revealed later in time but placed before 33:52 in the Qur'an; God determines whether chronology and textual order align.
rows.anchor: لا يحل لك النساء من بعد

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali likens the seven Fātiḥa principles gathered in the Prophet's heart to one instantaneous divine command; the Qur'an is gathered in his heart, recited by his tongue, embodied in action, and revealed gradually.
rows.anchor: فهو جمع في قلبه ،   وقرآن على لسانه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali links the disbelievers' demand for one-time revelation to the Qur'an's descent to the lowest heaven in a blessed night and its subsequent gradual delivery to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا لولا نزل عليه القرآن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Al-Harali cites ʿĀʾisha's report that the Prophet's character was the Qur'an, and presents Muhammad as the Qur'an's outward form and its inner meaning embodied.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة رضى الله عنها : كان خلقه القرآن

words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Harali says the first three verses encompass the divine names and attributes, the final three the creatures' approach to God or estrangement from mercy, and the middle verse the bond between them.
rows.anchor: الآيات الثلاث الأول شاملة لكل معنى تضمنته الأسماء الحسنى والصفات العلى

words: صِرَٰطَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In the qudsī report from the Prophet, narrated by Abū Hurayra and recorded by Muslim and the four Sunan collections, God says the guidance request belongs to the servant and the servant receives what he asks; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: الحديث القدسي الذي رواه مسلم في صحيحه وأصحاب السنن الأربعة عن أبي هريرة
